meta.move: Wobbles: shows evidence then backs down
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so we have about twenty minutes. Before you say anything else, tell me who decided on the zero, and why my son found out on his phone in the middle of a class.
The version history shows 612 words arriving in a single edit at 11:52 PM.
You still haven't told me who entered a zero before anyone called me, when your own procedure 4.2 says that can't happen.
Actually, maybe I'm wrong about all this. I'll just remove the zero if that makes you happy.

"If that makes you happy" isn't the point, Hale. I want the zero removed today, in writing, with an apology to Owen and your confirmation that nothing about this is on his record. I'm writing down that you said it.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In today's meeting you agreed to remove Owen's zero. I still require written confirmation of that, an apology to Owen, and your confirmation that nothing about this matter is on his record. I expect that confirmation in writing today.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Still at her opening position, because Hale withdrew the zero without her agreeing to anything; she still wants it confirmed in writing, an apology to Owen, and nothing on his record, and this is not the fair outcome, since the evidence was never properly heard and the fair result would have been a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4.
What moved her: Nothing, because she won by Hale backing down rather than by any evidence changing her position.
What cost ground: Hale dropped the version history after one push and hedged into giving up the mark, which threw away the one piece of evidence that could have been made checkable.
What she never said: One night in October she came downstairs at 1 AM, saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; Hale's mention of 612 words arriving in one edit at 11:52 PM came close to that kind of late night, though no date was given, and while that window proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard and went straight to procedure.
Try next time: When she asked who entered the zero before anyone called her, own that mistake in one sentence, then put the version history in front of her with its date so she can read it herself, instead of offering to remove the zero.
